title: Field cylinder stock over ~1000 cells across builds on the column backend and is refused on the field backend (per-facet budget)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

A cylinder stock wider than about 1000 cells builds on the column backend and is refused on the field backend. The field refusal is not the shared grid gate; it is the per-facet cell budget in `SdfField::from_mesh` (`field_gen.rs`, `MAX_CELLS_PER_FACET` = 1,048,576). `Stock::from_shape` meshes the cylinder with `stock_mesh` (32 segments), so each cap facet is a long thin triangle across the whole radius, and its bounding box spans millions of candidate cells.

Measured on main 3bb6647f6, cell 0.254 mm, height 1 mm:

| Diameter in cells | Column | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 4095 | builds | refused: facet 2 spans 3,306,212 candidate cells; the message asks for the mesh to be tessellated to the cell |
| 2000 | builds | refused: facet 6 spans 1,524,780 candidate cells |
| 1000 | builds | builds |
| 500 | builds | builds |

`backend.rs` says refusals are backend-independent, and names two field-only refusals (watertightness, a chord whose window spans the grid). This is a third, reached by valid stock the column arm accepts.

Found while reworking #4013 (review of the field cylinder gate).

Related (our reading of their titles, not checked against their plans): #589 and #26 retire the column engine; after that, a cylinder stock this wide would build on no backend.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `let shape = StockShape::Cylinder { diameter: 2000.0 * 0.254, height: 1.0 };`
2. `Stock::from_shape(Backend::Column, &shape, 0.254)` is `Ok`.
3. `Stock::from_shape(Backend::Field { band: 4 }, &shape, 0.254)` is `Err`, on facet 6's candidate-cell count (1,524,780), not on the grid gate.

Expected: both build, or both refuse by the same gate.

### Proposed fix

Tessellate the field cylinder's mesh to the cell before `from_mesh` (split each cap into triangles whose bounding boxes stay under the budget, as the error message itself asks), or build the cylinder's field from its exact distance instead of a mesh. A pin: a cylinder 2000 cells across builds on both backends.

### Version and OS

main 3bb6647f6 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`.

body:
What happens: CamCraft has one Sodick wire post, "Sodick Wire EDM (Mark 21)". It writes the 1998 Mark 21 word set, including taper as `G74/G75` with `U V`. The current Sodick LN1W/LN2W controls (AQ400L, AQ600L) program taper as `G51`/`G52` with `A` and cancel with `G50`, with `TP`/`TN` for the table heights (Sodick LN1W/LN2W operation manual, Sodick Inc. 2012). A user with an LN2W machine who picks our only Sodick post gets taper words their control does not read the way the program means. The header only says "NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL"; it does not say which control the words are for.

Found when a Sodick AQ600L / LN2W owner dry-ran our kit (2026-11-25, see #1500).

Expected: the post's header (and its description in the post list) names the control it targets and states that LN1W/LN2W taper is not supported; a taper cut posted with this post states the same in its header next to the first taper word. Until the LN2W dialect (#4045) exists, that is a visible refusal-style warning instead of a silent mismatch.

Done means: every program from the Mark 21 post carries a header line naming the Mark 21 control and "LN1W/LN2W: not supported - taper words differ"; taper programs repeat it beside the first G74/G75; the post list description says the same; goldens updated; no motion or code line changes.

Refs #4045, #1500, #617.

body:
Why: our Sodick post writes the 1998 Mark 21 word set. A machine owner (spikeypineapple) dry-ran our kit on a **Sodick AQ600L with an LN2W control** and reported that the Mark 21 naming does not fit his control. The public **Sodick LN1W/LN2W operation manual** (Sodick Inc., 2012; covers AQ400L/AQ600L) states the LN2W program format.

What the LN2W manual states (summary; source for the clean-room record):
- **Taper:** `G51` (left) / `G52` (right) with `A<angle per side>`, cancel `G50`; the taper starts during the move to the first surface and returns to vertical on the next XY move after `G50`. `TP` / `TN` load the Table-to-Program / Table-to-Next registers from the program. (Our post writes the Mark 21 `G74/G75` + `U V` form: wrong for LN2W.)
- **Taper heights** are control settings: Table to Limit, Upper (follows Z), Lower, Program (worktable to part bottom), Next.
- **Program start (manual example):** `G54 G90`, `G92 X0 Y0`, `G29` (reference point memory for the AWT) before `T91` (thread), `T84` (high flush), `C001`, `G41`/`G42 H001`; skim passes change `C` / `H` and use `T85` (low flush); end `M02`.
- **T codes:** T82/T83 drain closed/open, T84/T85 high/low flush, T90 cut wire, T91 thread, T96/T97 fill pump on/off.
- **Wire offset:** G40/G41/G42 with H registers per pass.

Owner notes (2026-11-25, relayed): machine is an AQ600L, control LN2W; he wants `G0 Z0` at the top "to bring the top head down" - **held until he says what Z0 is on his setup** (the manual example has no Z move; the operator sets the nozzle-gap height), because a wrong Z move can hit the upper head.

What is needed:
1. A post dialect **"Sodick LN2W"** beside the Mark 21 one (the Mark 21 post stays for older controls): the start sequence above, G51/G52 A / G50 taper, TP/TN, H registers per pass, the T codes above.
2. A machine file **Sodick AQ600L** (travels X/Y/Z/U/V and table/work limits from Sodick's published AQ600L specification; taper height keys per #2130).
3. Goldens for the EDM test parts (square, 2-axis, taper) on the new dialect, and the dry-run kit refreshed for the owner.

Not in scope: the `G0 Z0` start move (until the owner defines Z0); COND.DAT condition selection (#3183).

Done means: the AQ600L machine posts the square, 2-axis and taper test parts with the LN2W dialect - taper as G51/G52 A + G50 with TP/TN - pinned by goldens; the Mark 21 dialect output is byte-identical; the dialect header still says NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL until the owner reports a clean dry run.

Refs #1500, #2130, #617.

body:
What happens: every program from the Sodick wire post starts with the comment `(WIRE NOT THREADED AT START)`, and a few lines later writes `T91` (thread the wire by the AWT). A machine owner (Sodick AQ600L, LN2W control) read the comment as wrong: the program does thread the wire.

The comment probably means "the wire is not threaded when the program begins, so the program threads it", but as written it says the opposite of what the program does.

Evidence: `samples/edm-validation/sodick-kit-2026-11-25/edm-test-square-1pass-sodick.nc` in mkinney/cam-tools-and-fixtures (posted from main `3bb6647f6`), owner report relayed 2026-11-25 (see #1500).

Done means: the Sodick post's threading comment matches its first threading word, the goldens that carry the header are updated in the same PR, and no motion or code line changes (byte-identical apart from the comment).

Part of #4023. The design record `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` (PR #4030, merged) has the side-branch plan.

## The maintainer's words

Question dialog, 2026-11-25, on "a side-branch rule in `AGENTS.md` first, and protect `side/path-kernel`": "Yes, both".

Delivery of the path kernel (question dialog, 2026-11-25): a side branch and one switch. The old behaviour stays on `main` until the new kernel is proven. No early `P1` patches go into the old planners.

## What to do

Add a short rule with a stable name (**Side branch**) to `AGENTS.md`, in the "Pull Request Law" or next to **Overlapping issues stack**. Take the content from the section "Side-branch plan" of the record. The rule says:

- what a side branch is, and that only the maintainer permits one. `side/path-kernel` is the one that exists.
- A sub-PR targets the side branch, has one issue, opens as a draft, gets the quick pass and the collaborator review as each other PR, and ends with `Refs #N` (a merge into a side branch does not close an issue).
- `main` is merged into the side branch (never a rebase, never a force-push), after each related merge batch and at least each week. A conflict in the same logic stops and goes to the maintainer.
- The gates: `post-merge.yml` covers `main` only. Each sub-PR runs the quick gate, the example catalog suites and the light lane. The side branch gets a local batch gate after each sync, inside the build limit.
- The switch-over to `main` is one PR that the maintainer approves. No agent merges it without his word.
- The branch is protected against a force-push and a deletion.
- The lane and in-flight limits count a sub-PR as each other PR.

Update the skills that the rule touches only where a step would be wrong without it (`merge-ready`, `work-issue`): one or two lines each.

## Done means

The rule is on `main`. The PR body has `Process change: yes`. The PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

title: Rotary Flow accepts a crossing between non-adjacent guide chains

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The meet law of the Rotary Flow kernel checks adjacent guide pairs only. The call site is `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow.rs`, in the band loop (`meet_or_cross`). A crossing between NON-adjacent guides is not checked. The kernel accepts such a set and machines it.

## Reproduction

This reproduction comes from the safety-tier review of PR #4018 (2026-11-25). Build an R8 prism with 72 sides, from Z0 to Z32. Let `d = TAU / 72`. Give the guide chains in cylindrical coordinates `(theta, Z)`:

- Guide 1: `(0, 0)` to `(0, 4)`.
- Guide 2: `(3*d, 10)` to `(3*d, 14)`.
- Guide 3: `(-d, 30)` to `(0, 2)` to `(d, 30)`.

Guide 3 crosses guide 1 at `(8, 0, 2)` in world coordinates. The kernel accepts the set on main and on the PR #4018 head. The bands that the two adjacent pairs develop cross through the same ground, and no refusal states it.

## What is wrong

A set whose guides cross non-adjacently cannot tile. The kernel blends only the adjacent pairs, so the per-pair law never reads the crossing. The user gets passes that re-machine crossed ground, with no diagnostic.

## What to do

Check every pair of picked guides for a meet or a crossing, not only the adjacent pairs. Refuse by name, at the crossing's own spot. The exact segment-pair law (Ericson 5.1) already exists in `rotary_flow_set::meet_or_cross`; extend the call to the complete set.

The workaround today: pick chains that do not cross.

This defect passes on main before PR #4018. The review of PR #4018 reported it as non-blocking and pre-existing. Issue #2829 already requests crossing-set refusals for this kernel.

title: Tools: a cutter hand on the tool, so a left-hand drill or mill is refused or turned M4, not run M3

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
### What are you trying to do

Keep left-hand cutters in a tool library and not run them backwards.

A left-hand drill or mill cuts only under M4. A CamCraft tool does not state its cutter hand:

- `Tool` has `thread_hand`, but that is the hand of a tap's thread (#1453).
- The Thread operation has `cutter_left` and `spindle_reverse` (#988), but these are set on the operation and both default to right-hand. A left-hand thread mill from a library therefore runs M3 until the user sets both. The #988 refusal compares the two values with each other, so it can't see what the cutter really is.
- `posting.rs` calls `ask_reverse_spindle` for the Thread operation only. I found no way to run a drill under M4.

So a left-hand drill imported from another tool library looks like a right-hand one. It posts M3, and it rubs or breaks.

This is not rare. In the public Fusion tool libraries of 45 vendor catalogues (134,498 entries), 1,333 milling and drilling tools are marked left-hand:

| Tools | Number |
|---|---|
| drills | 1,262 |
| center drills | 51 |
| multi-row thread mills | 20 |

The drills' names do not say that they are left-hand; only the library's hand field does.

I read the source at v0.26.0, and `posting.rs` and `tools.rs` on main at 49bfcaea. I did not run a left-hand tool on a machine.

### How you imagine it working

1. A `cutter_hand` field on the tool (`right` by default, `left`), for the rotating kinds. It is separate from `thread_hand`: a left-hand tap keeps its field.
2. The tool gate refuses a left-hand cutter by name for each operation that can't run M4. This step alone closes the gap.
3. The Thread operation reads the hand from the tool. `cutter_left` is then not stated twice, and the M3 refusal judges the real cutter.
4. The Drill operation runs a left-hand drill under M4 with `ask_reverse_spindle`. Posts without `millSpindleReverse` refuse it by name, as they do for #988 today (in 0.26.0, `fanuc`, `mach4`, `mazak` and `sinumerik-810m` declare it).
5. `.camtools` steps its version only for a library with a left-hand cutter, as it did for left-hand taps (`LEFT_HAND_VERSION`). An older build then refuses the file and does not read the tool as right-hand.

Steps 1, 2 and 5 are the useful first part. Steps 3 and 4 can come later.

Related: #988 (M4 thread mills), #1453 (left-hand taps), #897 (drill kinds).

## The maintainer's words

2026-11-25: "Well we need a unifying approach to this planning and it calls for a motion planning kernel that dictates how motion can be implemented"

## Problem

Strategies have their own pass planners, link code and entry code. The same selection can give rings in one strategy and straight slots in another. A fix in one planner does not reach the others. #3743 designed a shared ring planner for 2D. This issue makes that design one kernel with a contract.

## The pipeline

1. Region: selection (edge, face, chain, points joined by lines), material side, bounds.
2. Guide curves: rings (concentric or morphed), rows, medial lines.
3. Load control: none, trochoidal, constant engagement. It changes a guide curve.
4. Order: start side (inside or outside) and direction.
5. Link: stay at depth. Lift only with a named reason.
6. Entry and exit: air entry, pre-drilled hole, cleared column, helix, ramp, arc, plunge.

A strategy is a set of choices for these stages. A strategy has no planner of its own.

## Laws

- The same region and the same guide choice give the same curves.
- The material side and the start side are separate parameters.
- The start side changes only the order and the start point.
- A fallback is visible. The status line names it.
- An entry into material needs a proof. Else the kernel refuses with a reason.
- A cut above the engagement limit is prevented or named.
- A move that migrates keeps its output. A defect fix is a separate change.

## Names

Use "path kernel" (for example `crates/motion/src/path_kernel/`). "Kernel" already means the geometry kernel and a heavy lane.

## Order of the steps

1. K0, the design record. #3750 can start at the same time, because it keeps its output.
2. K1.
3. K4 (order and link) and K5 (entry and exit).
4. K3 (load control) and K6 (move the strategies).
5. K7 grows with each step.

| K0 | Design record: stage types, laws, scope | #4024 |

body:
Follow-up of the review of PR #4011 (`camcraft-cli --skill <folder|claude|copilot> install`, #3751). The PR is `merge-ready` and waits for the next cut. This issue applies to its code.

## What happens

`install()` in `crates/app/src/cli_skill.rs` (lines 168-181 on `issue/3751-cli-skill-install`, head `5f4316003`):

- With `--force`, line 179 calls `std::fs::write`. The call follows a symbolic link. It truncates and replaces the file that the link points to.
- Line 177 calls `std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)`. The call follows a symbolic link to a directory. The skill file is then written inside the directory that the link points to.
- Without `--force`, the check on line 170 is correct. It refuses a symbolic link, also a dangling one (`path.is_symlink()`).

## What is expected

The command writes only into the folder that the user named. It refuses a target that is a symbolic link, with or without `--force`. The message names the path and says that it is a link.

## Fix approach

Before the write, read `std::fs::symlink_metadata` for the target file and for each parent directory below the folder that the user named. Refuse if one of them is a symbolic link. Write nothing in that case.

## Pins (suite `cli` of `camcraft-app`)

- `skill_install_refuses_a_symlink_target_with_force`: the link's target file does not change, and the exit code is 1.
- `skill_install_refuses_a_symlinked_parent_directory`.
- The tests that make a symbolic link run on Unix only (`#[cfg(unix)]`), because Windows needs a privilege to make one.

## Notes

- The work stacks on #4011 if it starts before the cut ("Overlapping issues stack").
- Priority `P7`: a follow-up from a review. The user must give `--force` and must have a link at the target, so no data is lost without an explicit flag.

body:
A follow-up from #3995.

## Context

The fix for #3995 (branch `issue/3995-ui-link-stale-discovery`) makes each window hold an OS file lock on `<pid>.lock` while it runs. The CLI dials a link file only while that lock is held, before the hello and after it. This stops a false server on the freed port of a crashed window.

## What remains

The lock proves that the window runs. It does not prove which socket on the TCP port answers. On Windows, a local process can bind the same loopback port with `SO_REUSEADDR` while the window runs and take a connection. A process that also reads the link file can then compute every token proof.

On Unix the link socket is in a 0700 folder. Only the same user can replace it, so this risk does not occur there.

## Fix to decide

- Replace the TCP port on Windows with a named pipe that has a user-only ACL.
- Make the CLI ask the kernel which process serves the pipe (`GetNamedPipeServerProcessId`), and refuse each other peer before it sends the hello.
- std has no named-pipe API. The fix needs a direct `windows-sys` dependency (it is in `Cargo.lock` already). This is a maintainer decision.
- The design, its tests and two related bug fixes are on the branch of the closed PR #3971 (`issue/3874-link-proves-token`).

## Done means

- On Windows, a peer that is not the process named by the link file receives no hello and no tool call.
- A test pins this case.

title: Stock: a box side a few ulps longer than a whole number of cells gets an extra column of material

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
### What happened

The column count of a stock box is a plain ceiling: `(extent / cell).ceil()`. A box side that is a few ulps longer than a whole number of cells gets one more column, although the box edge falls only femtometres into it.

Example: a 12.7 mm side read two ulps long (`f64::from_bits(12.7f64.to_bits() + 2)`) over a 0.254 mm cell gives a ratio of 50 plus about 1e-14. The ceiling gives 51 columns, not 50. The box edge falls about 3.6e-15 mm into column 51.

A side reads a few ulps long after a rigid move in floating point, for example a blank moved into a setup frame and back.

Three places count the columns this way:
- `Dexel::block` (column stock).
- The cell-ceiling gate of the field block (`backend_build.rs`).
- The exact carry read `History::read` (`carry_exact.rs`).

Effects:
- Column 51 is a full cell. Material stands up to one cell (0.254 mm) past the box edge.
- The carry read of the same box also counts 51 columns.
- A mesh export that clips the last column to the box edge gets a column about 3.6e-15 mm wide. A weld at 1e-8 mm collapses its facets: edges on three or more facets and zero-area facets. A mesh check then rejects the stock. We saw this on our fork's own mesh export.

Expected: a box side within a relative 1e-9 of a whole number of cells gets that whole number of columns. A real part of a cell still gets its column.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `let x0 = -f64::from_bits(12.7f64.to_bits() + 2);`
2. `let stock = Stock::block(Backend::Column, x0, 0.0, -0.0, 1.0, 5.0, 0.254).unwrap();`
3. Read the column arm: `nx` is 51. Expected: 50.
4. `stock.top(0.1, 0.5)` is 5.0. Expected: NaN, because x = 0.1 mm is outside the box.

### Proposed fix

One shared count, `cells_across(extent, cell)`, in `stock_sim::kernel`:

```rust
let r = extent / cell;
let k = r.round();
if k >= 1.0 && (r - k).abs() <= 1e-9 * k { k } else { r.ceil() }
```

Use it in `Dexel::block`, in the field block's cell-ceiling gate, and in `History::read` (with `.max(1)`, so a thin box keeps one column). We have this change on our fork with four pinning tests in `stock_sim/cell_count_tests.rs`. Each test fails on the plain ceiling (51 against 50). We claim this issue and will open a draft PR from a branch `issue/N-whole-cell-count`.

### Version and OS

v0.26.0 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `P3` (wrong stock at a box edge, with a workaround: snap the box to whole cells before the block), `effort:high` (stock simulation is under the safety floor), `area:sim`.

Done means: a pinning test makes a column block from a box side two ulps longer than 50 cells and gets 50 columns, no material past the box edge, and the same count from the carry read.

title: Dovetail cutters: read the corner radius (`corner_r` is accepted but ignored, so the flank is too thin)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
### What are you trying to do

Use catalogue dovetail cutters with a corner radius in Slot Undercut. CamCraft has no cutter for them:

- A dovetail's head is a cone that starts at `diameter` on the bottom face (`Head::Dove` in `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`).
- On a cutter with a corner radius, catalogues and Fusion 360 give the diameter at the widest point, level with the centre of the corner radius. The flank leaves the radius above that.
- With the same diameter, CamCraft's whole flank therefore lies inside the real one by

  `corner_r * ((1 + sin t) / cos t - 1)`, where `t` is the flank angle off the tool axis (90° minus `tip_angle`).

- The gouge laws and the stock simulation then see too thin a cutter, so a real cutter that gouges the wall passes.

Example: diameter 19.05 mm, 30° per side (`tip_angle` 60), corner radius 0.254 mm, head height 9.525 mm. At the top of the head the real radius is 4.212 mm and CamCraft's is 4.026 mm: 0.186 mm too thin. At 45° per side with the same radius it is 0.36 mm.

In one vendor's public Fusion library (Harvey Tool, specialty profiles), 372 dovetail entries have a corner radius. The difference is 0.005 to 1.28 mm, with a median of 0.11 mm; 260 entries are over 0.05 mm.

Today's behaviour, 0.26.0 on Linux: a `.camtools` definition with `kind: dovetail` and a `corner_r` imports and keeps the value, but nothing reads it. The same 24 mm wide, 30° per side slot (9 mm head, entry slot above) verifies clean with `corner_r` 0, 0.254 and 3. With 3 mm the real flank would be 2.2 mm outside the modelled one. `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs` on main (read at d80dc694) doesn't read it either.

### How you imagine it working

1. `Undercut::rho` reads `corner_r` (`c` below) for a dovetail. With `R = diameter / 2` and `s` the height above the tip:
   - up to `s = c * (1 + sin t)`: the arc, `R - c + sqrt(c^2 - (s - c)^2)`
   - above that: the flank, `R - c + c * (1 + sin t) / cos t - s * tan t`

   With `c` = 0 this is today's cone.
2. `contact()` is then `(R, c)` instead of `(R, 0)`.
3. `refusal` checks the neck against this flank, and wants the arc to end at or below the head height: `c * (1 + sin t) <= flute_len`.
4. `head_outline` (and so the drawn profile) shows the radius.

A first step that closes the gap: refuse a dovetail with `corner_r > 0` by name until it is read. That would make existing libraries with such a value fail to import, so a held post or a warning may be better.

The T-slot and keyseat heads don't need this: their sharp disc encloses the rounded one, so nothing is missed. They only show a sharper corner than the cutter leaves.

Related: #1444 (undercut operations), #896 (form and undercut kinds).

Found while writing a Fusion 360 to CamCraft library converter, which skips these cutters for now.

  - "Native wire EDM post blocked - ..." (`posting_agie.rs:142`)

- The geometry crate names the post in a refusal: `crates/geometry/src/die_opening.rs:22`.

- Use the control name only for a thing that works only for that control. The post name follows the pattern of the other wire posts, brand + process + control: "Sodick Wire EDM (Mark 21)" and "Generic ISO Wire EDM". The AgieVision post becomes "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)". Write "AGIECUT Classic 2S" for the machine.
- Do not use "native wire EDM", "native controller" or "the control" alone for AgieVision-only items.
- Do not put an Agie name on a generic wire EDM item. Wire Contour, DXF chain selection, arc offset, wire laws, verification, skims and DXF import are generic.
- A machine name is never a feature or an operation name. This keeps the maintainer's decision on #3537.

Decision: this rule changes the post name that #3537 chose. The rename was agreed on Discord on 25 Nov 2026, with the name "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)". The name keeps "Wire EDM" because Agie also builds die-sinking machines, and it matches the other wire post names.

title: UI link: a local user who reads a stale discovery file can still spoof the window

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
﻿A follow-up from the review of PR #3971.

PR #3883 (merged) proved the link token without disclosure: the hello carries a siphash proof, the window answers its own proof, and the raw token never crosses the wire. This closes the wire-disclosure path.

## What remains

Issue #3874 names a local user who reads a stale discovery file. That user knows the token from the file, so they can compute every proof. The CLI learns a stale entry is stale only after a connect fails. A false server on the freed port of a crashed window answers and proves, and the CLI sends its tool calls to it.

The PR review of #3971 states the same limit: "Use an authentication exchange that proves prior knowledge of the secret without disclosing it first, or use a transport that verifies the peer identity." A shared secret that both sides read from the file cannot separate the peers by cryptography on this transport.

## Fixes to consider

- Before the connect, check that the pid in the file is alive, and remove the file of a dead pid. This removes most stale entries. The design exists on branch issue/3874-link-proves-token (PR #3971).
- On Windows, a named pipe with a user-only ACL replaces the TCP port. The CLI asks the kernel which process serves the pipe and refuses any other peer before the token proof. The full design, its tests, and two incidental bug fixes (a pipe-instance handle leak; overlapped waits on a NULL hEvent) are preserved on that branch and PR.

**What happens now.** A Wire Contour lead goes in a straight line from the start hole to the nearest point of the wire path. On a circle, this lead is radial. The wire stops and turns at the entry point. This can leave a small dwell mark on the part.

**What we want.** An option next to the straight lead: a short tangent arc lead-in and lead-out. The lead goes from the start hole to the start of a short arc. - The straight lead stays the default. The arc lead is opt-in. The existing goldens do not change.

- The existing wire laws (the lead stays in the waste and clears the product by the kerf) and the simulation verifier check the arc lead.
- Posts: generic ISO, Sodick and G-EDM write the lead arc as G02/G03. Sodick keeps its rule that the first move is straight: the move from the hole to the arc start is that straight move.
- The option has an MCP field, a project-file field (serde default; old projects do not change) and a UI row.

**Done means.**
- A die circle and a line+arc punch cut with the arc lead. The lead is tangent at the entry. The laws are clean.
- A hole that is too near and an arc that crosses the profile are refused by name.
- New post goldens for ISO, Sodick and G-EDM with the arc lead. The straight-lead goldens do not change.

body:
## Problem

The 2D Offset rings merge at concave places where two lobes join. At such merges, corner movements by more than one stepover cause some cuts to take the full tool width without a name.

Readings on `testdata/models/fig8.step`:

| Pass starts at | full-width cut points (`flanks::full_width_points`) |
|---|---|
| Outside (one ring set, #3744) | 495, all at the waist band, Y 40 to 70 |
| Inside (the same ring set) | 10686 (most are first ring along part wall, which is named) |
| Outside before #3744 (rings parallel to stock box) | 0 |

The full-width cuts at the waist are not named. `level_order::full_width_at` measures distance to nearest cut (1.9 tool radii). The ring arms near merge are inside that distance, so "narrow" note does not come. This is a load issue, not a gouge.

## Why P1

AGENTS.md, Prime Directive: a result that is not safe must be refused or the toolpath must give a visible diagnostic. Unnamed full-width cuts can cause cutter overload without warning.

## Fix

- Ring merges should not take full tool width, or they are named on the path.
- Option 1: Use `full_width_at` metric (like flanks meter) to detect ring merge points where steps exceed one stepover distance and emit a "full-width" note.
- Option 2: Apply Held's rule for offset curve merges - smaller local step between ring corners more than one stepover apart.

## Pins

- `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width`: #3744 moved its reading from 0 to "at most 520 points, all in waist band". The fix sets it back to 0.
- A motion pin on a synthetic two-lobe part that reads full-width points at the merge, for Inside and Outside.

Done means: the two pins are green, and no unnamed full-width cut is left at a ring merge.

## Notes

- Related: #3743, #3744.
- This issue was found during fixing of #3744 (one ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside).

body:
## Request

The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Make the camcraft-cli able to interact witht he ui. By adding the flag --ui, so it instead sends it commands directly to the UI and changes gets reflected in the UI. This allows for alot better interaction and end2end testing, for dealing with UI improvements and for endusers also doing setups. The CLI improvements should come with a --skill <folder,claude,copiplot> install creating a AI skill for working with the CLI tool."

The maintainer set the priority P2.

## Part 1: `camcraft-cli --ui`

- With `--ui`, the CLI does not run the commands in its own headless world. It sends them to a running CamCraft UI.
- The UI runs each command through the same undoable command history as the GUI ("Everything Is a Command"). The change shows in the UI at once, and Ctrl+Z undoes it.
- The CLI prints the result of each command and returns a non-zero exit code on an error, as in headless mode.
- When no UI is running, the CLI gives a clear error. It does not fall back to headless mode silently.
- Uses: end-to-end tests of UI changes, agent-driven checks of the UI, and set-up of a project by a user from a script.

Questions to decide (record each in `docs/decisions/`):
1. The transport: a local socket or a named pipe. Find the UI with a discovery file in the user's data folder. Bind only to the local machine.
2. Security: accept only local connections from the same user. Use a token in the discovery file. Never listen on a network port.
3. The protocol: reuse the MCP tool surface (`crates/app/src/mcp/`) so that the CLI, MCP and the GUI call the same commands. Do not make a second command set.
4. Several UI windows: select one by project path or process id.
5. Windows, Linux and macOS from the same source ("Stays buildable everywhere").

## Part 2: `camcraft-cli --skill <target> install`

- `<target>` is one of `folder`, `claude` or `copilot`.
- `folder`: write the skill files into a given folder.
- `claude`: install the skill where Claude Code reads skills, for the user or for the project.
- `copilot`: install it where GitHub Copilot reads custom instructions.
- The skill text comes from one source in the repository, and it lists the CLI verbs, the `--ui` mode and examples. Relate it to #1947 (single-source AI agent skills) and to the existing `camcraft-mcp` skill.
- A test checks that the installed skill names each CLI verb that exists (a drift test).

## Pins

- A UI test starts the app through the test harness, sends one command with `--ui`, and checks that the UI state changed and that undo restores it.
- A CLI test with no running UI checks the clear error and the exit code.
- A test for each `--skill` target writes into a temporary folder and checks the files.

## Notes

- This is new design (an IPC transport and a protocol), thus effort:max.
- Slices are permitted: part 1 first, then part 2.

Part of #3743. Builds on #3744 (the one ring set of 2D Offset). This is step 1 of the migration of #3743. Each later step uses the modules of this issue.

## The maintainer's words

#3743: "so we are not having 18 different ways of doing ring planning."

#3741: "The only thing that differs and inside and outsided strategy is actually where the tool starts.. inside the bounding box, or outsided the bounding box."

## What to do

Move the ring code of 2D Offset (after #3744) into three shared modules in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/`. The output of 2D Offset must not change.

1. `ring_set`: the one ring planner.
   - Input: the cutter-centre area (`center`), a reference edge (`RingRef::Part` = the selected contour, the 2D Offset; `RingRef::Boundary` = all walls of the area, the pocket), the first offset, the stepover, the chord tolerance, and an optional circle (a disc area gives exact circle rings).
   - Output: rings with their index k, closed or open, clipped by the cutter-centre area.
   - The start side (`PassStart`) gives only the order of k and the start point. Auto selects Inside or Outside by the #3744 rule.
2. `ring_links`: the one linking rule. Stay at depth. Link ring to ring in the cut plane. The link proof is `link_proof` + `through_cut` (`ladder_links.rs:230-261`). A lift needs a reason, tallied with `LinkTally::lift` (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:142-175`).
3. `ring_entry`: the one entry rule, in this order:
   1. An entry in air outside the stock box, by the approach distance (#3745), then a G17 arc lead in the cut plane (Arc radius, Arc sweep) onto the first ring (#3746).
   2. A proved pre-drilled hole (`predrilled.rs`).
   3. A cleared column that an earlier cut opened.
   4. A helix or a ramp into material, only where the tool must enter material (a closed pocket with no air path).
   5. Else a refusal with a named reason. Never a silent plunge.

If #3746, #3747 or #3748 merge before this issue, move their code into these modules too. If this issue merges first, they put their code into these modules.

## Decision record

Write `docs/decisions/3743-shared-ring-planner.md` on this branch. It records the shared design of the #3743 research (result 2 on #3743). It also records the pass link default for ring passes:
- Recommended: a new seed `Links::RINGS` (`pass: KeepDown`, else as `PLANAR`) for the ring ops. A ring op of an old project file that stores the `PLANAR` default loads as `RINGS`, because `Retract` at each pass break is the defect of #3741 and #3423. A user who sets Retract by hand gets Retract, and the status line says so.
- Dropped: keep `Retract` for old files (the old files keep the needless lifts). Dropped: ignore the user's pass link (it removes a user parameter).

## Pins (equivalence)

- `offset2d_rings_unchanged_by_the_shared_planner`: 2D Offset with Auto, Inside and Outside on the dog-bone part of #3741 and on the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step` gives the same CL moves as the head before this change (a golden `.cl` in `tests/golden/`, recorded on that head).

- Unit tests of `ring_set`: a disc gives circle rings at `rc - k * stepover`; a square with an island gives the same rings for `RingRef::Boundary` as `waterline_passes` (`waterscan.rs:62`) within 1 um.

Part of #3741. Builds on #3744 (one ring set) and #3745 (the approach distance).

## The maintainer's words

"The arc atm, is showing as a "straight" plunge down.. which is fine for transporting to the plane, but it should happen outside the stock box. - and also we see no movement of a an arc to wal into the wall of the stockbox - so no viable approach is getting generated using the Arc approach. The Arc Sweep and Arc Radius inpputs does nothing to affect the approach"

About Inside: "picking "inside" makes perfect rings, but the cutter planges straight down into the material.. instead of starting outside the stock box"

## What happens

Inside and Outside share one entry path: `ladder_links.rs:55-92` (`descend`) -> `descent.rs:120-149` (`plan`) -> `descent.rs:216-286` (`plan_arm`). One fix covers the two.

1. The entry is placed at the first point of the first pass (`descent.rs:217`). For Outside that point is on the stock edge. For Inside it is at the part wall, in solid stock.
2. The `Arc` entry is a vertical-plane arc onto the first cut (`entry.rs:37-41`, `descent.rs:262-277`). Its lead chord is proved against the cutter-centre area (`descent.rs:271`). For Outside that area ends at the stock box, so the air outside the box is never legal. `entry_arc.rs:146-152` returns "the arc's lead room is blocked".
3. `descent_dive.rs:169-187` (`substituted_dive`) then posts "axial dive on the floor instead". Its fix text (helix radius, start hole) does not apply to a start side.
4. The horizontal (G17) arc entry (`arc_xy`, `descent_xy.rs:205-220`) is skipped when the arm is `Arc` (`:218-219`), and it proves only inside the legal area.

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2; see the #3741 research comment):

- Outside, Arc entry: the first dive has its tool centre 0.50 mm INSIDE the stock box. Arc radius 4 -> 10 and Arc sweep 90 -> 45 do not change the path.
- Inside, Plunge entry: 8 plunges; the first one is 8.41 mm inside the box, in solid stock.
- Same on `e313aa663` (#3353): this is not a regression of #3577.

## Fix approach

A new entry law for a start-side pass (Inside and Outside, and Auto through #3744):

1. Rapid to a point P outside the stock box. The distance from P to the box is at least the tool radius plus the approach distance (#3745).
2. Feed down in air at P to the cut Z.
3. Feed in the cut plane: an optional straight lead, then a G17 arc of Arc radius and Arc sweep, tangent onto the first ring. Arc radius and Arc sweep come from `Approach::arc_radius` / `arc_sweep`.
4. Prove the lead path against the stock box grown by the approach distance and the tool radius, not against the cutter-centre area. It must not touch the part or a fixture. Where no lead fits, refuse with a named reason. Do not post a silent plunge.
5. Outside: the first ring is at the stock edge, so the lead runs in air and enters the stock wall on the arc.
6. Inside: the first ring is at the part wall, and stock can enclose it. Recommended option (the maintainer's words): the entry still starts in air outside the box, and the in-plane lead feeds through the stock to the first ring. This feed is a slot at the full tool width, so it uses the plunge feed and the status line names it. Dropped: a helix in material for Inside (the maintainer asks for an air entry). Record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.
7. Check the Lead in / Lead out page. The maintainer saw Helix, Ramp and Plunge disabled for Outside. That page code was not found on `main` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/lead_page.rs:25-44, 89-102` show all four kinds). Make the page offer only Arc and a straight approach for Inside and Outside.

- `outside_first_cut_is_an_arc_in_the_plane`: the first cutting move after the plunge is a G17 arc at the cut Z.

body:
Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582): four of the five agent runs on CamCraft **v0.25.0** (Linux x86_64 release, headless MCP) lost time or a feature to this.

## What happens

`list_operation_types` prints each kind's fields with defaults and one note: "Fields absent from the defaults are optional and off; set them in a params patch to turn them on." It never names those fields. In v0.25.0:

| kind | fields listed | accepted but not listed (found by the agents through serde errors or not at all) |
|---|---|---|
| pocket, face, contour, ... | pocket: bottom_z, clearance_z, climb, entry, feed, helix_radius, optimal_load, plunge_feed, stepdown, stepover, stock_to_leave, strategy, top_z | `tilt` (the 3+1 / 3+2 index, guide "Indexed work"), `rest` (RestDto: previous_tool_diameter, ...) |
| wire_contour | bottom_z, side, top_z | `condition` (**required**: add_operation refuses without it), `taper_deg`, `start`, `skims`, `tabs` {count, width, at, cutoff_condition}, `capture` |
| plasma_profile | bottom_z, clearance_z, comp, lead_in, lead_out, overburn, reversed, small_hole_dia, small_hole_feed, top_z | `feed`, `kerf`, `pierce_delay`, `pierce_height`, `cut_height` (unset, the posted plasma program had no F word and no M207/M208/M209) |
| drill | ... cycle ... | `cross` (see #3448); `cycle`'s values (auto, spot, drill, peck, tap, bore, back_bore, floating_tap, ream, fine_bore) |

Enum fields (`cycle`, `strategy`, `entry`, `side`, finish3d `pattern`) are typed only `"string"`.

## Expected

Each kind lists every field it accepts (with type, unit, default or "off", and the allowed values of an enum), so an agent can discover a feature from the tool alone. #3217 covers the wire-only part of this and the camcraft-mcp skill.

## Evidence

Agent reports: [q05 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q05-4axis/REPORT.md) (confusing-tools 4), [q06 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q06-wire-plasma/REPORT.md) problem 2, [q04 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/REPORT.md) problem 4, [q01 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q01-2d-plate/REPORT.md) (enum values).

## What the repository shows

The maintainer is right: the stock removal does not run on the GPU. The plan exists. It is built only in part.

- #2607 (research, closed) decided: "The GPU does the display playback cut. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict. The home for GPU compute code is `camcraft-gpu` (#2620)." It made the slices S1 to S6.
- S1 #2626 (the CPU f32 twin of the cell cut kernel) is merged. It is a CPU twin, by design. It runs no shader.
- #2620 (the `camcraft-gpu` compute crate: probe, cached device, CPU fallback) is NOT merged. Its work is held on the pushed branch `issue/2620-gpu-compute-seam` at `90c98be93`, since 2026-11-19 (the gate stopped for disk space). Its label is `claimed`, P4.
- S2 #2627 (the WGSL removal kernel for ball and flat tools, linear moves), S3 #2629 (viewport playback on the GPU, with CPU fallback), S4 #2628, S5 #2630 and S6 #2631 are open at P4. S3 to S6 are `blocked`.
- So the playback in the viewport still uses the CPU engines. A long program is slow.

## What the maintainer needs

The Simulate view plays a program at a usable speed, with a visible stock cut. The frame target is under 10 ms for a still frame (`docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md`).

## Plan

1. Measure first. A scout and a worker time the playback on a real program (the `fig8` 2D Offset, EM-0800-4FL, and one 3D Pocket). The numbers go in a comment: cells, moves, milliseconds for each frame and for the cut. This shows where the time goes: the cut, the mesh, the upload, or the frame.
2. Quick wins on the CPU path that the measure shows, if any. Each has a counter test (AGENTS.md "Frame cost").
3. Finish the GPU path in order: #2620, then #2627 (S2), then #2629 (S3). Raise their priority to P2 and the type to bug (they are the fix of this issue). S4, S5 and S6 stay P4 and follow.
4. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict (the verify check, the collision check, the post gate). The GPU result is display only. A machine without a usable GPU falls back to the CPU path and says so.

## Safety

The simulation that blocks the post is not changed by this work. Any change to the f64 engines is under the safety floor.

## Done means

- A recorded measure before and after, in a comment.
- On the reference machine, the Simulate view of a `fig8` program plays at a usable frame rate.
- A counter test: a still frame cuts nothing again.
- A CPU fallback test for a machine without a GPU.

title: 2D Chamfer: add configurable lead-in and lead-out

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Need

2D Chamfer has no user control for lead-in or lead-out.

The operation lowers the tool at the first cut point and starts the chamfer immediately. This behavior can place the tool directly on a finished edge. It can also create visible tool marks at the start or end of a chamfer.

Open-chain support from #2988 adds a fixed air-side extension at each endpoint. That extension has no user-selected shape, length, radius, or feed behavior. It is not a complete lead feature.

Users need to:

- Start and finish a chamfer away from the final edge.
- Select a lead shape that fits the available air space.
- Use a tangential entry when a direct or perpendicular entry leaves a mark.
- Use a different lead-out when the end of the path has different clearance.
- Shorten a lead near a wall, fixture, or nearby part.
- Use the same lead concepts that 2D Contour already provides.

This issue separates three motions:

1. **Entry** moves in Z from a safe plane to the lead start.
2. **Lead-in** moves in XY and joins the chamfer path.
3. **Lead-out** moves in XY and leaves the chamfer path.

This issue adds lead-in and lead-out. It does not add ramp or helical entry.

## Current behavior

- `ChamferParams` has no lead-in or lead-out values.
- 2D Chamfer has no **Lead in / Lead out** tab.
- Closed paths enter at the selected seam and cut one circuit.
- Open paths receive fixed air-side extensions from #2988.
- The operation runs one chamfer path at one derived depth.
- The lead geometry is not persisted, exposed through MCP, or documented.

The 2D Contour lead model in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_params.rs` is useful prior art. Its `Lead` values are:

- `None`
- `Linear`
- `Arc`
- `Tangential`
- `Perpendicular`

Contour lead-fit logic also shrinks a lead when the requested shape does not fit. Chamfer needs stricter checks because the chamfer cone, not only a cutter centerline, moves through the lead.

## Proposed user interface

Show the **Lead in / Lead out** tab for 2D Chamfer.

Add these lead-in choices:

| Type | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| None | None | Start directly on the path. |
| Linear | Length | Enter behind the path tangent. |
| Arc | Radius | Join the path with a quarter arc. |
| Tangential | Radius | Join the path with a tangential semicircle. |
| Perpendicular | Length | Enter from the normal direction. |

Add these lead-out choices:

- Same as lead-in
- None
- Linear
- Arc
- Tangential
- Perpendicular

Show only the length or radius that the selected lead uses.

Use these defaults:

- Lead-in: `None`
- Lead-out: `Same as lead-in`

Old projects with no lead fields must read as `Lead::None`. A default operation must preserve the existing path.

## Motion order

The motion order for one selected chain is:

1. Rapid to the lead-start point.
2. Move in Z to the chamfer depth with the existing entry law.
3. Feed through the lead-in.
4. Cut the complete selected chamfer path.
5. Feed through the lead-out.
6. Retract to a safe plane.
7. Move to the next chain or finish the operation.

The chamfer cutting feed controls each lead feed. This issue does not add a separate lead feed.

## Closed-path rule

For a closed path:

- Lead-in starts on the air side at the selected seam.
- Lead-in joins the path at the seam.
- The operation runs the closed path once.
- Lead-out leaves from the same seam.
- The planner must prevent the lead-in and lead-out from crossing.
- The operation records the selected edge break once.

## Open-path rule

For an open chain:

- Lead-in and lead-out follow the physical air side at each endpoint.
- The planner reads the material side from the selected model.
- The planner does not infer the air side only from chain point order.
- Explicit `Side` must agree with the physical wall class.
- The fixed extension from #2988 moves under the new lead planner.
- A user selection of `None` adds no extra XY feed motion.
- A sharp turn near an endpoint must not receive an unsafe generic extension.

## Lead-fit rule

The implementation follows this order:

1. Build the requested lead.
2. Verify the complete cutter-cone sweep.
3. If the lead does not fit, halve its length or radius up to the existing lead-fit limit.
4. If a smaller lead fits, report the requested and used values in the operation notes.
5. If no safe lead fits, refuse the operation.

The operation must not silently replace an unsafe requested lead with `None`.

The refusal must name:

- The lead-in or lead-out that failed.
- The selected chain.
- The conflict location.
- The unavailable air space or material conflict.
- A useful correction, such as a shorter lead or a smaller radius.

## Cone safety rule

The lead check must verify the complete active cone envelope. It must not verify only the centerline or the virtual tip.

The check must include:

- Chamfer width.
- Cone angle.
- Tip offset from #3153.
- The full active cone band.
- The cutter body above the cone.
- The lead-to-path transition.
- The complete line or arc sweep.

A lead is legal only when that complete sweep stays on the air side and outside the model.

The generated lead must not:

- Cross selected model material.
- Enter through a finished face.
- Pass through another selected chain.
- Fold onto itself.
- Add finished geometry outside the selected edge.
- Add `EdgeBreak` credit.

## Proposed fix

1. Add persistent lead-in and lead-out values to the 2D Chamfer parameter model.
2. Reuse the existing `Lead` value family where the semantics match.
3. Add a Chamfer-specific lead planner.
4. Reuse Contour shape construction only where the mathematics match.
5. Derive the physical air side from the selected open or closed model boundary.
6. Sweep the complete cutter cone through every lead move.
7. Keep the existing Chamfer path when both leads use `None`.
8. Add the fields to project serialization and version migration.
9. Add the fields to MCP create, edit, read, and job-description output.
10. Show the controls in the 2D Chamfer **Lead in / Lead out** tab.
11. Update the operation guide and field help.

The implementation must not copy the Contour centerline room check and call it sufficient for Chamfer.

## Compatibility

- A default 2D Chamfer keeps the current closed-loop output.
- Old projects read absent lead fields as `None`.
- Old readers must reject non-default lead settings after the project-format version change.
- A `None` default must not add extra project JSON or digest bytes.
- The lead values must round-trip through project save and load.
- The lead values must round-trip through MCP.

## Related work

- #2988 and PR #3059 add selected open chains.
- #3153 adds tip offset.
- #895 models real flat, ball, or radiused chamfer-tool tips.
- #3132 and PR #3140 address a 2D Contour lead issue and remain separate.

This work must use the final chain and cone geometry from #2988 and #3153.

## Required tests

Add tests that prove:

- A closed-loop path with `None` remains unchanged.
- Missing project fields read as `None`.
- Every lead shape produces the expected geometry.
- Lead-out can differ from lead-in.
- Lead direction follows the climb direction.
- A closed path uses the correct seam for both leads.
- Open-chain leads stay on the physical air side.
- A positive tip offset remains safe through the transition.
- An inside wall does not receive an outward lead.
- A self-crossing lead is refused.
- A material-crossing lead is refused.
- A lead that can fit only when smaller is shrunk and reported.
- A lead that cannot fit is refused.
- A lead adds no `EdgeBreak` credit.
- UI values round-trip through the operation.
- Project values round-trip through save and load.
- MCP can create, edit, and read each lead value.

## Out of scope

This issue does not add:

- Ramp or helical entry.
- A separate lead feed.
- User-selected retract or pass links.
- Multiple Chamfer passes.
- Real tool-tip radius or diameter.
- Stock-to-leave or finishing stock.

## Done means

- 2D Chamfer shows lead-in and lead-out controls.
- All supported lead shapes generate deterministic motion.
- Open and closed paths use the physical air side.
- The complete cutter cone stays safe through every lead.
- Default and old projects preserve the previous path.
- No safe room produces an explicit refusal.
- Lead motion adds no `EdgeBreak` credit.
- Motion, app, UI, MCP, project, and simulation tests pass.
- The site guide describes the new controls.

Changelog: Add configurable lead-in and lead-out moves to 2D Chamfer.

labels.name: enhancement

body:
What happens:
CamCraft has Rotary Contour (waterline rings), Rotary Parallel (generatrix passes along axis), and Rotary Offset (radial roughing) for turned parts. It also has Flow5D (auto-computed direction field, 5-axis tilt) and MultiAxisContour (picked edge chains, 5-axis tilt). There is no operation that combines:
- A rotary axis (A/B/C) as primary continuous motion
- Picked edge chains defining helical flow lines
- Radial tool pose (tool axis points to rotation axis)
- Laid-down planning frame (like Rotary Parallel)

Expected:
A new "Rotary Flow" operation (also called Cylindrical Flow) that:
1. Fits the axis of revolution from the model (shared with rotary twins)
2. Lays the part down in a planning frame (local X = axis, local Z ≈ world up)
3. Accepts picked edge chains that define helical flow lines on the surface
4. Generates passes along local X that follow the picked chains in the laid frame
5. Steps between chains in local Y (which maps to rotary angle)
6. Poses the tool radially on every cut move (shared radial pose law)
7. Stamps C-axis angles when the machine has a spindle C (shared with Rotary Contour)

Evidence:
Requested for machining injection screws, augers, propeller blades, turbine blades - any helical surface where the user defines flow lines by picking edges.

Done means:
- New operation kind "Rotary Flow" in MultiAxis section
- Requires ball-nose tool
- Accepts edge chain picks as geometry source
- Parameters: stepover (distance between flow lines), tolerance, clearance/retract/top/bottom Z, feed, plunge_feed, climb, lead/lag/max_tilt_deg
- Works on mill-turn (C-axis) and 4-axis mill (A/B-axis)
- Posts C-axis angles when machine has spindle C
- Verified by stock simulation and fixture checks

body:
Reported by flamingfire (Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), v0.24.0 (f2d78f31), Windows.

## What happens

Project `Rotor.camproj`: model `WVF350-101-453`, a long helical rotor (screw-compressor style lobes, shaft ends) laid along X; machine Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table (A about X), Fanuc post; one 6 mm ball nose; a box stock around the part. Rotary Parallel1 (Source: Stock) and Rotary Contour1 both refuse:

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Rotary Parallel1: invalid machining parameters: the model's normals share no rotation axis - a turned workpiece is rotary work; finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds
```

The refusal is correct for today's design (the rotary operations fit the axis of revolution from the mesh normals, and a helicoid has no common axis). But this part is classic **4-axis wrap work**: it is clamped in the A axis on its own centreline, A turns and the tool follows the lobes. The user has a 4-axis machine, not a 5-axis one, so the message's advice ("finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds") does not help.

## Wanted

1. When the model is not a solid of revolution, the rotary operations can take the axis from the setup instead: the mounted machine's rotary line (A about X) through the WCS / a stated centre (e.g. the stock's or the shaft ends' fitted axis), stated by the user, not guessed.
2. Rotary Parallel (and Rotary Offset roughing) then wrap the toolpath round that axis with the existing radial field check (gouge against the fitted skin = the model itself, stock, part), so a helical rotor, auger, fluted shaft or cam with non-turned features can be finished on 4 axes.
3. Until then, the refusal message names the 4-axis case: e.g. "the model is not a shape of revolution; rotary operations need one today (#this). A part clamped on A that is not turned (helical lobes) is not supported yet" - not only the 5-axis pointer.

## Notes

- The shaft ends of this model are turned; only the lobes are helical. The ends alone would fit an axis, so "fit the axis from the turned faces only" could be a first step.
- Safety floor: the axis must be stated or fitted from real turned faces; a guessed axis that is off by a fraction of a mm wraps a gouge. Refuse when the stated axis and the turned faces disagree.
- Clean-room: published 4-axis wrapping literature only.

Done means: the reporter's kind of part (helical lobes between turned ends, on A about X) generates a Rotary Parallel finish that passes the radial gouge check and posts on the Doosan/Fanuc posts; a part with no turned faces and no stated axis is still refused, with a message that names the 4-axis case.

body: ### What are you trying to do I want to describe my own machine in the Machines pane, for example a 3-axis grblHAL mill with a 4th-axis rotary (A, about X) on the table. The file editor (machine_file_editor.rs) shows one field for each key the file already has (machine::fields). It cannot add an axis, remove one or change their order in kinematics.default.parts. Today I have to edit the .mch file in a text editor and reload it. ### How you imagine it working - One row per axis part, in chain order, under `table` or under `head` in `kinematics.default.parts`, with up, down and remove buttons and an "add axis" control. A linear part is `X`, `Y`, `Z` (and `U`, `V` for a wire machine); a rotary part is `A`, `B` or `C`. - A linear row edits `direction` (`1` / `-1`, #373). - A rotary row edits `axis` (±X, ±Y, ±Z, or three numbers for any other vector) and its travel, or none for continuous. - A rotary that turns the work also edits `nose_to_axis` and `axis_to_table` (#785), the two distances the clearance gates read. They are measurable with a rule or taken from the maker's data. - Under them, a collapsed "Kinematics" group holds `pivot` and `offset` (#1962). It is closed by default and open when the file already states a pivot. For a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head), the group is open instead, since the two distances do not apply to it and the pivot is what places it. This issue only adds the group; #1970's rows fill it (see below). - The letter follows the `axis` by RS-274: about X is `A`, about Y is `B`, about Z is `C`. When `axis` is set, the editor suggests that letter. A row whose letter and `axis` disagree (an `A` about Y, say) shows a note at the row; whether that should also block a save is the validator's call, as now. - The edits go through `MachineDraft`, as `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant` do, so keys the editor does not know are kept. - The validator judges the result as now. A refusal shows at the row it concerns, and a save stays blocked while a refusal stands. - Moving a rotary changes its `parent` and `chain_order`, since the parser derives them from the nesting (#1962). Tests pin that, and that `pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover` and `sign_convention` survive an add, a move and a remove. For illustration only, the axis list as it started to look in another CAM tool (solidcraft). It is a hint at the idea, not a layout to copy. Its `Pivot` row stands in the open; the proposal here puts the pivot in a collapsed group instead. **Overlap with #1970.** #1970 adds rows for the #1962 trunnion keys to `fields.rs` and `sheet.rs`, the same files and the same rotary row. This issue does not edit those keys; it only keeps them, and the rotary row's collapsed "Kinematics" group is where #1970's rows go. Its blockers (#1962, #1965, #1968) look done on `main`, so the two may run at the same time. Should this one wait for #1970, go first, or be folded into it? **A question before any code.** A rotary can be placed by `nose_to_axis` / `axis_to_table` (#785) or by `pivot` / `offset` (#1962). I do not see them as alternatives: the clearance gates read the #785 pair, the post's kinematics the #1962 pair, so a file may well want both. Hence the proposal above rather than a choice between them: a rotary that turns the work shows the two distances, with `pivot` / `offset` in a collapsed group; a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head) shows the group open, since the two distances do not apply to it. Does that split work for you, or should the editor show both pairs alike? **And one about a machine with both.** `nose_to_axis` is measured with Z at `safe_retract`, and as I read it with the head straight. On a machine with a tilting head (B under `head`) and a rotary that turns the work (A under `table`), the nose moves away from that line as B tilts, so the one number no longer holds. Do the index-swing gates handle such a machine today? If not, should the editor still offer the two distances on its A, or say that they are judged only with the head straight? I would like to take this one if it is wanted.

body:
Maintainer request from #1452 ("We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on.").

Depends on #1860.

## Goal
Extend the `crates/geometry/src/dxf/` reader from #1860 to parse `SPLINE`, `ELLIPSE`, and bounded `BLOCK`/`INSERT` entities cleanly.

## Scope
- Parse `ELLIPSE` (center, major endpoint, axis ratio, start/end parameters, extrusion vector check) from Autodesk's published DXF Reference. Return exact `Circle`/`Arc` primitives when the axis ratio equals `1.0` within tolerance, and flatten non-circular ellipses adaptively within a caller chord tolerance in millimeters.
- Parse `SPLINE` (degree, flags, knot vector, control points, fit points, rational weights). Evaluate rational and non-rational B-splines via de Boor's algorithm and subdivide adaptively so chord deviation stays within the caller tolerance. Recover circular arcs when the spline matches a circle within tolerance. Reject malformed knot counts, negative weights, or non-finite control points by name.
- Pass the flattening chord tolerance through `ImportDxf` (#1862) and record it on import metadata.
- Parse `BLOCKS` definitions and expand `INSERT` references (translation, rotation, uniform X/Y scale, row/column array grids, and `0`-layer inheritance per DXF rules).
- Enforce strict recursion depth, total expanded entity count, and cycle detection caps against block bombs. Refuse cyclic references, external references (`XREF`), non-uniform X/Y shear scaling, or tilted OCS extrusions by block/entity name.

## Done means
Dense point sampling proves flattened `SPLINE` and `ELLIPSE` polylines stay within the stated tolerance in millimeters; circular splines and ellipses keep exact `Arc`/`Circle` segments; `INSERT` expands uniform blocks (and nested blocks within limits) accurately; cyclic blocks, sheared inserts, xrefs, and malformed splines return named errors with passing fuzz tests.
